AccountList.description: A single document, not `Page[T]`: bounded per device (proposed D22).
AccountList.title: AccountList

AppCreate.description: New apps are `active`; their default role is the built `<key>:member` (no input for it).
AppCreate.title: AppCreate

AppCredentialIssue.description: Optional issuance body; no body or `{}` means `manifest` (current clients keep working).
AppCredentialIssue.title: AppCredentialIssue

AppCredentialRead.description: Metadata only: never the secret, never the hash.
AppCredentialRead.title: AppCredentialRead

AppCredentialScope.description: One scope per key (ADR-0021 §1). USR-29 adds the first runtime scope (ADR-0025).
AppCredentialScope.title: AppCredentialScope

member_count.description: Distinct active users with at least one non-expired role assignment on the app (app scope or any org); unverified email counts; `admin` = staff (OQ5).
member_count.title: Member Count

AppUpdate.description: Partial update; `key` is immutable. Null only for the role ids.
AppUpdate.title: AppUpdate

AssignmentCreate.description:
Assign a role at app scope (`org_id` null) or in one organization; `granted_by` is never
input (it is the actor once ADM-002 lands).
AssignmentCreate.title: AssignmentCreate

EntitlementUpdate.description: An explicit `null` means no change; `limits` replaces the whole object.
EntitlementUpdate.title: EntitlementUpdate

ErrorBody.description: The error object of every non-2xx JSON response.

code.description: Machine-readable code, e.g. validation_error, unprocessable, not_found, conflict, unauthorized, permission_denied, rate_limited.
code.title: Code

details.description: Always present. A list for validation_error and unprocessable, an object for rate_limited and permission_denied, otherwise null.
details.title: Details

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

InvitationCreated.description: Identical whatever the target email is (no account/member oracle); never echoes it.
InvitationCreated.title: InvitationCreated

JoinPendingResponse.description: 202: the app needs a staff decision (`join_policy = approval`).
JoinPendingResponse.title: JoinPendingResponse

Jwk.description: OpenAPI only: the public members of one signing key.
Jwk.title: Jwk

LogoutRequest.description: Exactly one of `{account_id}` (that account) or `{all: true}` (the whole device).
LogoutRequest.title: LogoutRequest

ManifestMember.description: Narrows `<app>:member` to these permissions (never widens past the eligible set).
ManifestMember.title: ManifestMember

ManifestPermission.description:
One declared permission. `scope` is required on `org_mode = required` apps unless the
key is reserved (ADR-0015); an omitted `description` leaves the stored one.
ManifestPermission.title: ManifestPermission

ManifestRole.description: An extra role; additive (permissions are only ever added to an existing role).
ManifestRole.title: ManifestRole

MePermissions.description:
The caller's own admin authorization (USR-11, ADR-0008 amendment). A UI hint only:
the API enforces every permission. `admin:*` is returned unexpanded and matches every
`admin:` key (same rule as `permits()`). Additive within v1: new fields may appear.
MePermissions.title: MePermissions

OrgInvitationRead.description: Staff view of one invitation (USR-23). No invitee email, token, token hash or email HMAC.

status.description: Computed at read time on the database clock: accepted > revoked > expired > pending. An invitation can read pending while its inviter has since lost the right to invite; accepting it is then refused.

OrgInvitationRead.title: OrgInvitationRead

OrgMemberRead.description:
One org-scoped assignment with its holder (USR-23). `total` of the list counts
assignments, not distinct users: a user with two roles in the org appears twice.

active.description: Not expired (database clock); ignores user, org and app status, so not 'effective in tokens'.
active.title: Active

created_at.description: When the assignment was first granted; kept when an expired assignment is re-granted in place.
created_at.title: Created At

user_status.description: Account status; disabled users are listed.

OrgMemberRead.title: OrgMemberRead

PermissionCreate.description:
`is_admin` absent or null: false, except `<app>:*` and admin-app permissions, which are
always stored `true`. `scope` absent or null: the reserved key decides, else `org` on
`org_mode = required` apps and `app` otherwise (ADR-0015).
PermissionCreate.title: PermissionCreate

PermissionUpdate.description: Partial update; `key` is immutable. Explicit null is accepted only for `description`.
PermissionUpdate.title: PermissionUpdate

RoleCatalog.description: Public role catalog (D17). Field order is part of the ETag; append-only.
RoleCatalog.title: RoleCatalog

RoleCreate.description: New roles are never `is_system` and hold no permissions (use the PUT).
RoleCreate.title: RoleCreate

RoleDefinitionRead.description: Staff read model of a role (USR-16): any app, `admin` and disabled ones included.

is_default.description: This role is the app's default role (apps.default_role_id).
is_default.title: Is Default

privileged.description: App is `admin`, or the role holds a permission with is_admin. Granting or revoking it needs admin:* (ADR-0008 G4). UI hint; the server enforces on every write.
privileged.title: Privileged

updated_at.description: Last change to the role row (e.g. name); permission changes do not bump it.
updated_at.title: Updated At

RoleDefinitionRead.title: RoleDefinitionRead

RoleHolderRead.description:
One assignment of a role with its holder (USR-17). `total` of the list counts
assignments, not distinct users: a user can appear once per org and once at app scope.

active.description: Not expired (database clock); ignores user, org and app status, so not 'effective in tokens'.
active.title: Active

user_status.description: Account status; disabled users are listed.

RoleHolderRead.title: RoleHolderRead

RolePermissionsReplace.description: The role's full permission set; duplicates are ignored, `[]` empties the role.
RolePermissionsReplace.title: RolePermissionsReplace

RoleUpdate.description: Partial update of the display name; `key` and `is_system` are immutable.
RoleUpdate.title: RoleUpdate

UserRead.description: Admin view of a user. Explicit fields only: never `password_hash` (R11).
UserRead.title: UserRead

UserSessionRead.description: An active account session of a user, for staff (explicit fields only; USR-10).

device_last_seen_at.description: Browser last seen; refreshed at most hourly.
device_last_seen_at.title: Device Last Seen At

id.description: Account session id; the `account_id` apps send to /auth/token.
id.title: Id

ip.description: Recorded when this browser first signed in; shared by every account on it.
ip.title: Ip

last_used_at.description: Last sign-in of this account on this device.
last_used_at.title: Last Used At

user_agent.description: Recorded when this browser first signed in; shared by every account on it.
user_agent.title: User Agent

UserSessionRead.title: UserSessionRead

UserStatusUpdate.description:
Unlike `OrganizationUpdate`, explicit null is rejected (422).

Intentional, per USR-01b AC.
UserStatusUpdate.title: UserStatusUpdate

get.description:
One read-only document for the dashboard (counts only, no audit rows).

`members_per_app` also reveals every app's key and name, including disabled apps and
the `admin` app, so `admin:stats:read` exposes that app list without `admin:apps:read`.

Caveats: failed sign-ins include unknown emails (anonymous actor) but not requests refused with
429 or by Turnstile. Sign-ups include self sign-ups and CLI-created accounts and do not depend on
the audit log or its retention. Sign-ins are event counts over a rolling 24 h window, not distinct
users. Sign-ups cover the last 12 months in the `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` time zone; the last month is
partial. Members per app: distinct `active` users with a non-expired role assignment on the app
(app scope or any org). The counts are approximate (not one snapshot). Clients ignore unknown keys.

delete.description: Revoke all account sessions of a user, on every device. Revoking sessions stops the user from getting **new** access tokens (`/auth/token` -> 401 `session_invalid`) and ends the user's admin (`aud=admin`) tokens bound to those sessions on their next admin request. Tokens of other apps stay valid until `exp`, at most `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` (12 h in production) plus 30 s leeway. It does not stop a new sign-in with the password. IP and user agent are recorded when the browser first signed in and are shared by every account on that browser.
